description: P³C computes the minimal constraints of a simple temporal network (STN) only for the pairs that matter, not for all `n²` pairs. It first makes the constraint graph *chordal*, which means that every cycle of four or more points has a shortcut edge. To do this, it removes the points one by one, the one with the fewest neighbours first, and links the remaining neighbours of each removed point; it also tightens each such pair through the removed point (*directional path consistency*). A second pass in reverse order then gives every edge of the chordal graph its exact shortest-path distance, the same bound as the full minimal network. Use it on large sparse networks, and add a constraint without bounds for each extra pair that you need.

papers.authors: Léon Planken, Mathijs de Weerdt, Roman van der Krogt
papers.title: P³C: A New Algorithm for the Simple Temporal Problem
